root_cause.text: The kmalloc_nolock() context check on PREEMPT_RT was too narrow; it only excluded NMI and hard IRQ contexts, but failed to exclude other non-preemptible contexts (e.g., preemption disabled due to preempt_count > 0 from a tracepoint BPF program), leading to an attempt to acquire a sleeping local_lock in an atomic context.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff changes the check from `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT) && (in_nmi() || in_hardirq()))` to `if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT) && !preemptible())`. The commit message explicitly states: "the current check... misses the case where preemption is disabled" and "When a BPF program runs from a tracepoint with preemption disabled... kmalloc_nolock() proceeds to call local_lock_irqsave() which attempts to acquire a sleeping lock".

intent_record.how: Under PREEMPT_RT, the function now returns NULL for any non-preemptible context (e.g., spinlock-held, hardirq, NMI) rather than only hardirq/NMI, preventing a potential sleeping-in-atomic bug when local_lock is used.

    slab: Introduce kmalloc_nolock() and kfree_nolock().
    
    kmalloc_nolock() relies on ability of local_trylock_t to detect
    the situation when per-cpu kmem_cache is locked.
    
    In !PREEMPT_RT local_(try)lock_irqsave(&s->cpu_slab->lock, flags)
    disables IRQs and marks s->cpu_slab->lock as acquired.
    local_lock_is_locked(&s->cpu_slab->lock) returns
bic_trace_step.reason: In kmalloc_nolock_noprof, the PREEMPT_RT check only excludes NMI and hard IRQ contexts (line 'if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT) && (in_nmi() || in_hardirq()))'). It does not exclude other non-preemptible contexts like preemption disabled (preempt_count > 0), which can occur from tracepoint BPF programs. This omission allows kmalloc_nolock() to attempt to acquire a sleeping local_lock in an atomic context on PREEMPT_RT, which is the root cause.
